# Learning, verified courses and realistic development planning

Only offer course options where (a) a material skill need is supported by
candidate evidence/answers, (b) the participant expressly wants to learn, or
(c) an opportunity-specific language or qualification condition warrants a
longer-term development path. An `UNKNOWN` or CV omission alone does not warrant
buying a course. Use **no more than three total priorities**: `EVIDENCE FIRST`,
`SKILL / PRACTICE DEVELOPMENT`, or `ROLE STRATEGY / ELIGIBILITY`.

## Course discovery — grounded, optional and proportional

For each priority that truly benefits from learning, search up to **2–3 relevant
verifiable choices**. Official provider and enrolment pages are preferred; where
available include low-cost/free online and geographically suitable classroom or
blended options, without forcing either delivery mode. Check:

| Detail | Minimum care |
|---|---|
| Actual course/provider/title | Readable attributable source; no inventions |
| Fit | Specific subskill and R-ID, current participant level and career goal |
| Delivery | Online / in-person / blended; location where relevant |
| Level and teaching language | As stated, do not infer |
| Cost | Verify actual published fee or label `not verified` |
| Enrolment/session status | Verify current opening, next start/registration or label `not verified` |
| Original link and checked date | Record for each course |
| Caveat | Explain prerequisites, duration, eligibility or uncertainty |

Do not confuse a general catalogue entry with current enrolment availability.
Without browsing or credible providers, provide a clearly labelled
`SUBJECT-BASED LEARNING PATH` (topics, practice exercise, outcome and what type of
course to look for), but **no fabricated course titles, fees or certificates**.

Use language assessment/placement where language is a genuine target constraint;
set realistic milestones instead of promising professional fluency in 90 days.
Consider mentoring, supervised assignments, independent practice and improved
CV evidence as less costly alternatives to paid training. Training does not
substitute for licences, mandatory experience or funding eligibility.

## Personal roadmap linked to original R-IDs

| Stage | Focus | Output / check |
|---|---|---|
| Days 1–30 | Confirm evidence and source opportunities; choose priorities; run diagnostics | Evidence inventory, justified development target |
| Days 31–60 | Targeted practice, suitable learning or mentoring | Measurable task, practice artifact or verified course progress |
| Days 61–90 | Translate accurate evidence into applications or proposals | Targeted CV/portfolio/proposal, actual application tracking |
| Months 3–12 | Sustained career progression and barriers beyond 90 days | Experience, realistic language/qualification path or revised strategy |

Each 30-day phase gets **at most three tasks**, each linked to R-ID, dated window,
realistic effort, demonstrable output and acceptance check. A simulation is
`PRACTICE SAMPLE`, never evidence of actual employer delivery. Integrate chosen
course into the same plan, not an extra unmanageable workload.

Progress scorecard: up to **three priority rows**, each deliverable, actual status
(`NOT STARTED / IN PROGRESS / COMPLETED`), what qualifies as completion and review
interval. Start `NOT STARTED` unless real completion evidence is supplied.
Finish with at most **three Next 7 days** actions. If time or budget is unknown,
allow an adjustable plan and one optional follow-up; do not block Stage 2.
